subtitle: The slime becomes the adventurer

body: Dragon Quest Heroes: Rocket Slime is Tose's Nintendo DS action adventure starring Rocket, one of the familiar Slimes from Dragon Quest. His home of Boingburg has been attacked, and rescuing its inhabitants sends him through areas populated by the series' recognisable monsters. The adventure alternates overhead exploration with battles between enormous tanks. Its elastic hero supplies the connection between them: objects gathered during an excursion can become ammunition in the next confrontation. The small creature normally encountered by beginning adventurers becomes the resourceful centre of his own rescue mission.

Rocket's Elasto Blast charges a forward launch that strikes an enemy or object and sends it into the air. Moving beneath it allows Rocket to catch and carry it, with room for a small stack of items or creatures. Throwing provides another way to use what has been collected. Railway carts carry rescued Slimes and other discoveries back to Boingburg, linking exploration with the town's gradual recovery. The basic movement therefore supports fighting, gathering and rescuing, giving a simple elastic charge several useful consequences inside the same scene.

Tank battles move the action inside a mobile fortress, where collected objects are loaded into cannons and launched toward the opponent. The stock gathered while exploring becomes a practical resource, making the earlier choice to carry something home matter in a different kind of encounter. Rescuing Boingburg's inhabitants also brings new helpers and information back to the town. The two halves of the adventure continually support each other: a short outing produces people and supplies, and the next tank fight asks how well those discoveries can be put to work.
